Assistant: That's a real blocker: crates.io requires every dependency — including internal path deps — to carry a `version =` requirement, since published crates can't resolve local paths. Let me size this up across the whole workspace before deciding how to fix it.

Assistant: This is genuinely required infrastructure — not just for this rc but for any real crates.io publish — and it's 100% mechanical (adding a version constraint, no behavior change). I'll do it properly with a TOML-aware script rather than naive text replace, since some entries span multiple lines. [...] Assistant: Confirmed — dev-dependencies with a bare `path` are auto-stripped by cargo when packaging, so I over-scoped by touching them too, which created false cycles from legitimate test-fixture cross-deps. Fixing the script to only touch `[dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]`. [...] **Found and fixed (not yet merged):** the entire workspace had zero internal `nmp-*` path dependencies carrying a `version =` field — 320 lines across 59 crate manifests plus the root `[workspace.dependencies]` entry for `nmp-ownership`. This isn't specific to this rc; it was always going to block any real crates.io publish. Fixed with a TOML-aware script (hit and fixed a comma-formatting bug from the library along the way), scoped correctly to exclude `dev-dependencies` (which cargo auto-strips when unversioned — including those would have created false publish-order cycles, and I initially got that wrong before correcting it). Verified: `cargo metadata` resolves clean, representative crates compile, and `cargo publish --dry-run` on the real first-in-order crate (`nmp-ownership`) succeeds all the way to the upload step. [...] Assistant: That's expected and actually confirms the fix is real — `cargo publish --dry-run` validates against the live crates.io index, so any crate with an internal dependency will only pass once that dependency is actually live. `nmp-kinds` isn't a true leaf. Let me find one that is and confirm dry-run passes there.
